item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5359 designates a group of buildings in ████, USA. SCP-5359 consists of seven (7) buildings designated SCP-5359-01 through -07. A circular stone clearing with a 30 meter circumference is in the center of the building. Each of these buildings has a different anomalous property as listed below.

Deleted at -14 and three votes.

SCP-5311 Class: Euclid is a 9 year old girl who loves to make paintings. She is 4'3 in height and weighs 153lb. The girl has short black hair and a white dress down to her knees. She has 2 beaded bracelets on her right arm that are also white. Not to mention the fact that she has incredibly bad hearing and will have to resort to reading things off of a piece of paper when communicating with others. She is very sensitive to high pitched sounds. She has no known name and researchers has not found any info about her past yet.

Deleted at -14 and three votes.

SCP-5215 is a two-floor 15m x 10m wooden motel in the Malian part of Sahara Desert near the town of ██████. When a human being makes eye contact with the building, SCP-5215 becomes active. The human subject starts hearing their dead friends’ or relatives’ voices calling them from inside the motel. This attracts the human to enter although it is up to them to do so. There is no way to access the 2nd floor, what lies there is still a mystery. Inside, there are four seats, two doors and a counter. In the left door there is a small room with a chair which has limbless body with no inferior jaw and eyes.

Deleted at -13 and three votes.

item.title: Re: Anomalous-D
item.content:encoded:
I remain fascinated by the "possibilities" of this line of thinking

Sure, but there's no guarantee the audience will be similarly fascinated just because you are. Be careful not to confuse "intellectually complicated" with "interesting".

I have to admit, I find this confusing. I thought D-Class came off of death row. Who goes to death row but murderers?

This is a question you can answer on your own with a little research: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment#Capital_crime Suffice it to say, the assumption that only murderers are put on death row would be incorrect.

+ show block
– hide block

This describes him perfectly. And that he's repeatedly put in dangerous close contact with anomalies sounds like exactly what they're used for.

It seems like you're confusing a statement about all D-Class in general with handling of individual D-Class. D-Class as a whole may be exposed to tons of different anomalies, but that doesn't mean a single D-Class would be, especially one that is very likely to fail their regular mandatory psychiatric evaluations. Again, a super terrible attitude untrustworthy expendable lab rat is not as useful in a experimental procedures as a compliant, less expendable lab rat.

I do admit that I have no perspective on what people who have been immersed in it for years think of that particular anomaly,

The discussion thread for 682 has some recent comments on it. You can look at said discussion via the "discuss" link at the bottom of the page.

but as a new reader it honestly never occurred to me that it was in any way outdated.

As a general resource, you can look at the Top Rated Pages This Month listing: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/top-rated-pages-this-month These are more accurate examples of current site standards/quality expectations. Since we are currently in Series 6, not Series 1, Series 6 articles are a better representation of the current audience's preferences.

item.title: User05
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: ACS Header, basic layout, etc.

Elevator Pitch: A user on Discord that causes a person's existence to vanish

Central Narrative: The person in question is called "User05" on Discord, and the exact name + tag is censored. The only way to come into contact with the user is pure luck. He'll usually send a friend request (which should not be accepted).

When a person starts talking to User05, he'll seem normal at first, seemingly like he used to know them or they used to be friends. After about ten (10) minutes of talking, stuff starts getting weird.

  • Vagueness
  • Familiar pictures of the persons life
  • Misspelling
  • Faster typing
  • Spamming random letters
+ show block
– hide block

The victim might not see anything odd about it, just a casual troll on Discord. However, things get even stranger when he states the full legal name of the victim, age, and physical appearances. He sends pictures of the victim's face in various angles in random areas, as though he never knew he was being pictured. After this event, User05 goes silent for around 3-5 days.

After he returns, he claims that he knows where he lives, who he lives with, and will arrive there shortly. The first way of contact is through mail, which is a piece of paper that says "Hi. :) - Me"
If the victim continues to talk to the man on Discord, the SCP will speak in an unknown language, send pictures resembling satanism practices, etc.

  • Unknown language
  • Pictures of satanism
  • Spamming of the phrase "C0N9V3RT", followed by random symbols
  • Spam calls
  • Discord crashing

The victim will feel the sudden urge to block or unfriend the SCP after Discord crashes, and the urge can not be stopped no matter how much the victim denies it.

Blocking the SCP, or unfriending the SCP will just make things worse. If a victim does so, they will hear knocking on their front door directly after they unfriend/block User05. Their computer will crash, and all the doors in the house will lock (even if they don't have a lock on it). After the knocking stops, the door will open, and footsteps can be noticeable at this point, and get louder by the second, and faster, to the point where he's practically running. The footsteps stop at the bedroom door, but the door doesn't open. The light in the room will either explode or turn off, and the fan will turn on if it's off, or off it's it on. After the lights go out, the victim loses consciousness, and disappear out of everyone's life. However, after he goes missing, no trace of him will be left behind (SSN, birth certificate, any licenses, any proof of existence) as he just never existed in the first place. No missing posters, no sobbing relatives, nothing, he never existed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A cool anomaly that sort of follows the generic paranormal scheme, but it's detection is almost impossible as the victim's existence vanishes and no one knows who he is (as the people who do, don't exist).

item.title: SCP-XXXX My friend ED (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
The mind is a delicate thing, and when your life starts to take a turn for the worse and an SCP seems to be watching your every move, it might just break.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: A standard SCP file with a focus on a journal where the afflicted documented their experience with the SCP, contrasted with interview logs and reports from coworkers documenting their perspective on the afflicted's slow decent.

Elevator Pitch: Researcher exposes self to SCP-XXXX, a standard horrific monster. It doesn't seem like the SCP even notices her, until she starts to see it every time something goes wrong.

Central Narrative: The central narrative is a documentation of the Doctor's slow decent into 'madness.' As more and more things go wrong in her life, she ends up doing several self destructive things and perpetuating the cycle. All the while she sees this SCP every time something goes wrong. Everything from accidentally telling the person serving lunch to enjoy their food too to a fatal car crash that takes the lives of one of her coworkers.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main thing that I'm hoping to make different is to cause the reader to question the reality of what this researcher is experiencing. The whole point of the story is to cause the reader to wonder "Is the SCP causing this, or is it just there when it happens? Or is the SCP even there at all?"

Additional Notes: I know that the theme of questioning reality due to an SCP isn't exactly a new one, which is why I'm hesitant to even post this. But I have yet to see a concept similar to this so I was hoping that maybe there's still a market for a monster that just fucks with your mind. Or perhaps doesn't. Who really knows.

item.title: Re: -1
item.content:encoded:
I didn’t say it was a joke, I said the pacing wasn’t right to me. I was surprised the ending was “just like that”, if that makes sense.

In my opinion, in the nicest way possible, I can see you on the other side of the screen, writing this. Not a foundation researcher. The writer seems passionate and excited about this topic. It can have a happy ending, but maybe have them report things as

“The case [of the disappearance of the many koalas] was originally thought to be a massive poaching operation that would damage the ecosystem was dismissed, but when the events’ anonymous properties became apparent research into the disappearances quickly began.”

For me it needs to have that sense of, ‘a sad thing is happening and we don’t give squat about it until we can prove it fits under our strict criteria.’ That’s was missing for me in this piece. Some sad moments could make the happy ending have a larger impact.

And about being skeptical, you can go ahead and dismiss my advice as wrong but it is advice and I think you should take it and craft this SCP to be 1% better. People generally don’t like my SCPs and I feel kinda hated on the forum but I’m trying to help people and pitch ideas that haven’t been thought of yet. I’m gonna leave it here before it turns into a rant.

Good luck with your article.

item.title: Anomaly Zero (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Elevator Pitch: A devoid of facial features, humanoid-entity, gets confused by others as a Wight. However, it is not. This humanoid entity decreased the body temperature of an individual down to -5000°C that gets in contact within the range of a 20-meter circular area and can create snowstorms at the temperature of -5000°C also.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The Foundation acquired this anomaly when a group of tourists in Da Lat1 was found death and their body temperature seems to be below 0°C, as a witness claims that the only person who wasn't dead among all of the tourists was an individual wearing a black hoodie covering their entire face. As MTF-Gormity-10, "Ground Controllers" were deployed to detained the anomaly. However, several attempts resulted in failures until they've finally figured out its anomalous effects and successfully detained it in the next attempt due to not understanding its anomalous properties. Which after they've found out it is capable of speech.

The anomaly was designated as SCP-XXXX and classified to be a Keter Class anomaly. Based on the Foundation's logs, SCP-XXXX appears to have powerful latent thermal, cryokinesis, and snowstorm manipulation abilities that happen naturally. In one of the incidents, SCP-XXXX's anomalous properties accidentally produced a powerful energy force that almost frozen the entire facility and almost resulted in some SCPs and personnel being killed as the Foundation decides that SCP-XXXX will be detained in a standard humanoid containment chamber constructed out of tungsten and is furnished with in-organic furniture and two large heating devices that're at the temperature of 700°C, combining with the -5000°C of SCP-XXXX will not result in any problems, any personnel who enters its containment chamber won't feel too hot nor too cold due to the temperature being stable thanks to both of the heating devices and the freezing abilities of SCP-XXXX.

In some of the addendums, the Foundation has stated that SCP-XXXX's future experiments are performed in a special room separated far away from the Site. In SCP-XXXX experiments, it is shown that SCP-XXXX was observed to have high durability, intelligence in manipulating others, agility, and skill at weapon masteries, especially silhouette knives as it uses as long-range attacking weapons and also close-range attacking weapons. SCP-XXXX states that it has no clue of how it was able to do so.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An anomaly that freezes peoples to death within the range of a circular 20-meters.

Footnotes
1. A continent of Vietnam.

item.content:encoded:

Genre: Historical Science fiction

Page Layout: Description, followed by a long addendum

Elevator Pitch: A giant tree in Iraq that reaches into the stratosphere. Lammasu roost in its branches, attacking anything that attempts to ascend it. At the top, near the edge of space, the ruins of a bizarre structure can be found.

Central Narrative: In ancient Neo-babylonia, during the height of Nebuchadnezzar II's rule, a serum is developed in the labs of the Hanging Gardens that can wildly accelerate plant growth. Nebu II seizes the opportunity to create the world's first "space program": he builds a structure to be carried by a tree into the sky to pierce the "veil of heaven." This is revealed through a journal written by a pair of scribes, as they document the fantastic events both from above and from the ground.

Hook: The mystery of a giant cedar tree in Iraq should pique interest, leading readers into the world of anomalous ancient Babylon.

item.title: Re: some criticism
item.content:encoded:
The main thing the article has going for it, the code, is pretty cool, but it's not enough to carry the article. There are severe lapses in clinical tone, and mysteries generally rely heavily on the build-up and suspense, which this article has none of.

+ Spoilers ig
- 

The caeser shift (I think thats what its called?) is pretty clever and not something I've seen on here before, and stuff like ZJW-5329 give away that it's not just gibberish and keymashing (at least for me), but I don't think a single gimmick like that alone is enough to carry the whole article. There's no substance without that, no buildup to get the reader engaged, and I have to agree with Robert that the glitch section is a bit uninspired and the concept of 'thing that kills you' (because that's what you are presenting it as before someone cracks the code) is cliche enough to turn me off the piece.

Either way, you clearly have some cool ideas, I can't think of a code like that ever used on the wiki. If you're going to give it another shot, could I recommend reading some of the guides on http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/comprehensive-guide-hub (especially some of the misc essays) and going through the greenlighting/crit process on the forum to make sure you can make the best possible version of any idea that has a much better chance of surviving on the wiki.

Hey, recipient of the story here! I wanna say thanks, of course, for putting the time and effort into making this gift for me. I very much appreciated the content warning, as I didn't really expect such a violent story resulting from my prompt, but, having been warned, I was able to put myself into a mindset where I wasn't unpleasantly surprised by it. I'm intrigued by the underlying mystery here, and I think tales could spin off from this piece about the location, the McQueen family, and how the magic of the place and the actions of its inhabitants feed off of each other. That would be one way to side-step the violent mentally ill person stereotype as well, if it's hinted that Gabriel's violent tendencies are seeded by something anomalous in this place of his ancestry, something that influenced his father's connection to magic as well.

While I would be interested in seeing more stories branch off from this, I do have one request that I think I'm entitled to make: if Gabriel McQueen becomes a recurring character on the site, even just in one more piece, I would prefer if his first name were changed to something else. It was fun to read a story with "my" name in it, even given to a character whose actions I find abhorrent, and as long as it's clearly in the context of "this was a gift for this person," I'm fine with keeping it! But my username becoming a recurring character out of my control would be almost weirder to me than reading my actual legal name in an SCP. Hope you understand!

item.title: Re: SCP-XXXX "The Frozen Wood"
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for replying! The SCP is a geographical area that moves from place to place and yes, the bodies accumulated over the years. People can simply stumble upon the area and the bodies are scattered throughout since it doesn't kill instantly and it can take some time for its effects to become obvious to the victim. I'll change the part about the bodies being perfectly intact since, as you pointed out, it doesn't make much sense.

As for the narrative, I was originally going to have it explained via the people who come across it and as more people disappear it draws the attention of both the nearby populations and the Foundation. The SCP itself doesn't have much narrative or lore because its simply a natural phenomenon; It has no sapience, no intent to kill, but it has been around for some time, causing it to become a part of the folklore of the areas it commonly teleports to.

Something major that will be in the article however, is a failed attempt (due to faulty ventilation systems and lack of care, not competence, of the facility) at establishing a facility in the area, resulting in the deaths of nearly all personnel involved (All D-Class, most of the researchers), except of course, the higher-ups who are heavily protected. While not a massive setback for the Foundation, it proves as a harrowing example to go off of for future endeavors in the area and similar SCP's.

This was my Art Exchange forum review:

This is an MTF raid of a sarkic compound with an unusually festive twist right at the end (though in hindsight it was indeed hinted at). There are some pretty big breaches in what should be clinical tone, and not in the dialogue (where such things are accepted), and one instance of some messed up formatting, but besides these minor complaints, the tale is very fun. I like the background before the MTF (Tau-5, "Samsara) goes in to clear things out. I like the descriptions of the weapons they are armed with. I think the twist could have been a bit more hinted at — as is, when people read this story in the future, I think it will come out of complete left field — but if foreshadowed better could be exceptionally funny and creative. Pacing good, Samsara good (kind of creepy in how robotic they talked), lore good, tale good.

But this tale has changed! It even changed while I was still doing gift reviews, but I was caught up in other reviews, and then real life. Anyhow, I read it now, and damn, yes. This is a much better ending. The tonal shift is not so sudden, and despite clearly becoming festive it remains creepy and mysterious. Glad that the alligator was a reindeer (Rudolf, even?), as that otherwise felt like a random unnecessary detour. Anyhow, this is weird and goofy and great. +1

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A cactus that you can't be near for more than 20 s or else all your romantic relationships will end.

Central Narrative: A otherwise regular cactus, this SCP will only show it's effects after 20 or more seconds of exposure. After that, all your romantic relationships will end within a week. Amnestics do not help. Apart from not wanting to restore the relationship, no additional effects were found. Due to the nature of this anomaly, researchers are authorized to do civilian testing.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A SCP that makes you have divorce.

Additional Notes: found on a garage sale.
